title: GradBias: Unveiling Word Influence on Bias in Text-to-Image Generative Models

bias_targets.methodology: Dynamically proposing gender as a bias category using an LLM, generating images from neutral prompts, using a Vision Question Answering (VQA) model to classify the gender distribution of generated subjects, and measuring individual word influence by backpropagating the VQA loss to text token embeddings.

Evaluating racial distributions in images generated by Text-to-Image models using a VQA model. Word-level influence on racial bias is quantified by computing the gradient of the VQA cross-entropy loss with respect to the input prompt's word embeddings.

Assessing the age representation of subjects in generated images via VQA predictions, comparing the distribution against a uniform baseline, and tracing the bias back to specific prompt tokens using gradient-based attribution.

Discovering and quantifying open-set, non-demographic biases (e.g., laptop brand, train color, person attire, cake type) by leveraging an LLM to build a custom bias knowledge base from captions, classifying generated images with a VQA model, and calculating token gradients to explain word influence.
